cases.title: NYC DOT's leading pedestrian intervals on Lafayette Street

source.label: NYC DOT to Manhattan Community Board 2, April 28, 2026

cases.quote: Install left turn lane treatment: Plus, Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI): Prince St, Houston St, Great Jones
cases.question: Is each of the three intervals supported by its corner's own crash record?

results.label: Reconsider
results.why: the city's records show an interval already installed there (2024)

results.label: Compare first
results.why: backplates are expected to avoid 0.39 injury crashes a year, against 0.08

results.label: Proceed after a site check
results.why: the estimate holds only if a turning movement is confirmed; 13 injury crashes and 1 death in five years

proof: NYC's own signal dataset (xc4v-ntf4) lists Lafayette Street & Prince Street, installed 2024-10-11, and none at Houston or Great Jones
NYC's crash dataset (h9gi-nx95), by street names: 12 crashes with an injury and 1 with a death at Lafayette & Houston, 13 in all, as the tool says
cases.fixed: 6 faults this case found, all fixed the same day, among them a 2023 death the New York mapping missed
cases.cost: about $0.40 of model use for the whole case
